problem:
Consider the following parabola:

$$
x=-\frac{1}{4}{t}^{2},\,y=-\frac{1}{2}t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

The Cartesian equation of the parabola is

${y}^{2}=$
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =-4x,\,t=-2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =4{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=-4x$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{y}^{2} & =-4x \\ {y}^{2} & =-x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian equation of the parabola is ${y}^{2}=-x.$
